narrative:
The model estimates a 25% chance that you will fail your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

Three factors stood out as most important in this prediction. By far the strongest influence was your record of one past class failure. While students who passed had zero previous failures on average, your history of failing a class before pushed the prediction noticeably toward failing this year.

The second most important factor was your reason for choosing this school. You selected it because it was close to home. This choice actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward passing, since students who picked the school for location reasons tend to do better than those who chose it for other reasons.

Third, your strong desire to pursue higher education also helped reduce the risk of failure. Almost every student who passed shared this same ambition, so your clear goal of continuing your studies worked to counteract some of the risk.

To improve, focus first on preventing any further setbacks in your current subjects. With only one past failure on your record, turning things around now is very possible. Talk to your teachers about targeted support in the areas that caused problems before, protect your study time, and reduce the high number of absences you have had this year. These steps can still change the outcome before the final exams.
